question: Which urban local self government body manages small towns with limited municipal functions like street lighting and drainage?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Town Area Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A **Town Area Committee** is a semi-municipal authority responsible for administering small towns with limited municipal functions.
 
• It typically manages essential services such as **street lighting, drainage, and sanitation** in areas that are not large enough to require a full-fledged municipal corporation.
 
• These committees are constituted by the **State Governments** and operate under their supervision.
 
• Unlike municipal corporations, a Town Area Committee has **limited jurisdiction and fewer responsibilities**.
 
• The members of the committee can be either **elected, nominated, or both**, depending on state regulations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Municipal Corporation:**

 
 
• A municipal corporation is an urban local government body responsible for the governance of large cities with populations exceeding a specific threshold (e.g., 1 lakh or more).
 
• It handles diverse functions such as waste management, public transportation, and urban planning.
 
 
 
• **Special Purpose Agencies:**
 
 
• These are autonomous bodies created to manage specific functions like water supply, transportation, or housing in urban areas.
 
• They operate independently of the municipal government.
 
 
 
• **Port Trust:**
 
 
• A Port Trust is a specialized body responsible for managing and maintaining ports and their associated facilities.
 
• It primarily focuses on trade and maritime operations rather than urban governance.
 
 
 
• **Urban Local Self-Government:**
 
 
• Urban local self-government refers to the institutions that govern cities and towns, ensuring the provision of essential services and infrastructure.
 
• Examples include municipal corporations, municipalities, town area committees, and notified area councils.
